overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by giving insufficiently specific executive session purpose notice and at convening, but found the executive session purpose lawful, the ratification notice adequate, and no secret deliberation; ordered compliance and minutes release, and declined nullification.

allegations.summary: Complaint said an agenda item added at the October 12, 2010 meeting was not posted in advance. The AG reviewed the executive session topic wording and found it too vague.
allegations.key_passage: This notice falls short of the requirement that the Committee state "all subjects that may be revealed without compromising the purpose for which the executive session" will be called.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the added agenda item was improperly noticed because it did not state the board would vote to ratify a negotiated contract.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require the chair of a public body to anticipate whether a contract negotiation will come to fruition during an executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the executive session discussion did not qualify for any executive session exemption. The AG found the contract negotiation purpose lawful, including discussing a title change.
allegations.key_passage: We find that these types of discussions are an appropriate component of executive session deliberations for the purpose of conducting "contract negotiations with nonunion personnel."

allegations.summary: Whether the Committee gave enough detail about the executive session purpose both in the notice and when convening in executive session.
Complaint said members deliberated and decided in secret to create and fill a position. The AG found the superintendent's individual calls to members did not amount to a serial deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we understand that Superintendent Casey spoke with each committee member individually and did not convey the individual members' opinions to the other members.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Promptly release the executive session minutes from September 28, 2010 and October 12, 2010, if not already released.
remedy_passage: We accordingly order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. Furthermore, we order that the Committee promptly release the executive session minutes from September 28, 2010 and October 12, 2010, if it has not already done so, as the purpose for keeping those minutes confidential no longer exists.
